entries.statement: The next deliverable must be a concrete architecture and rollout plan suitable for later translation into AWKP tasks or Workflow B GoalExecutionRequests, not implementation code.
AHRA runtime, reusable workflow logic, validators, and generic CLI commands must be reused through the installable AHRA package and CLI rather than copied into target projects.

Target projects must own only a minimal local governance overlay: AGENTS.md routing, work/task state, project authority docs, project policies, machine-readable AHRA project and policy config, and project-local skills.

Project init and adopt must be separate commands: init creates the minimal overlay for new projects, while adopt is non-destructive for existing projects and reports conflicts instead of overwriting them.

The generated project overlay surface must be exactly AGENTS.md, .ahra/project.yaml, .ahra/policy.yaml, work/index.md, work/tasks/.gitkeep, docs/architecture/authority-map.md, docs/policies/project-policy.md, and .agents/skills/README.md.
.ahra/policy.yaml must be the machine-executed project policy authority; docs/policies/*.md must remain human-readable explanation only and must not be treated as the enforcement source.

Adoption templates must be packaged inside the AHRA package for now and must contain only project overlay skeleton files, not workflow runtime, AHRA source, legacy workflow modules, fixtures, or archive history.
Doctor must be strict for AHRA overlay health only and must not run target project business tests by default.

The plan must preserve the split between AHRA foundation invariants supplied by the installed AHRA version, project human-readable policy overlays under docs/policies, and machine-enforced project policy under .ahra.
The plan must not promote experimental Workflow A or any non-default component to a default route.
The plan must not claim AHRA is already a production-grade distributed orchestrator for arbitrary projects.
The plan must not silently choose unresolved product or project policy after Human Gate 1; any later policy expansion beyond this boundary requires explicit Human Gate approval.

Human Gate 1 is complete when the maintainer approves this boundary contract and a later planning increment can produce the concrete adoption architecture and rollout plan without open boundary questions.

Within this boundary, the later plan may choose document section structure, naming of internal plan subsections, and sequencing of rollout milestones, provided it does not add files, commands, policy authority, runtime defaults, or implementation scope beyond the approved boundary.

Within this boundary, the later plan may recommend bounded follow-up AWKP tasks or Workflow B GoalExecutionRequests for docs, policy templates, project config, CLI init/adopt/doctor behavior, and tests, but those tasks still require Human Gate 2 authorization before implementation.

turns.message: We need to formalize AHRA's future adoption model. My current direction is: AHRA core runtime/workflows/validators should be reused via installable package and CLI, not copied into every target project. Each target AI Agent project should get only a minimal local governance overlay: AGENTS.md routing, work/tasks state, docs/architecture authority map, docs/policies for human-readable project policy, .ahra machine-readable project/policy config, and project-local skills. Policy should be split into AHRA foundation invariants from the installed version, project policy overlays in docs/policies, and machine-enforced policy in .ahra. I want a concrete plan first, not code implementation yet. Surface any open decisions or tradeoffs for Human Gate approval, especially project init/adopt/doctor scope, exact generated files, policy placement, package vs template boundary, and how not to accidentally promote experimental Workflow A to a default route.
